text: OK so i see a problem here again. and its in the selection which is not even letting the uv update correctly. i have a cut in place, i have 1 side selected. lets do another cut. can you tell that there is a new cut? neither can i. but there is, evidently. but i dont see it. [Blockbench: the second cut updates the uv highlight AND the selection] also be very aware. it cut on the face only selected. it didnt reconsider it all as one face.
resolution: The second loop cut on an already-cut face was invisible (mesh, UV, and selection all unchanged), and it 'reconsidered it all as one face' instead of cutting the selected sub-face. Root cause: loopCutAxisInfo computed the cut span (lo/hi on the cut axis) from ALL mesh verts — the whole cube's 16-unit extent — not the selected face's. So a second cut on an 8-unit half still used the 16-unit range with a default offset of 8, placing the new plane exactly at the first cut's plane → no new geometry → nothing changed (so lcKeptFace returned the same face and the selection/UV didn't update either). Fix: loopCutAxisInfo now computes lo/hi from the SELECTED FACE's loop verts; new editMesh.ts loopCutRange(m,axis,lo,hi,cuts,offset) applies the cut within that explicit span (loopCut refactored to call it with the whole-mesh range for the bare-cuboid case). So a cut on a cut half now subdivides THAT half — visible, and the UV + selection update. editMesh 26/26 (added a test proving a sub-span cut adds faces while a whole-range cut at the existing plane is a no-op). Studio.tsx + full chain bundle clean. Hot-reload TSX, nothing committed. KNOWN REMAINING DIFFERENCE: cutMeshByPlane still splits the whole loop at that plane (the parallel faces), where Blockbench confines the cut to the single selected face — flagged as the next refinement (single-face cut) if the user wants exact parity.
